page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a burstable instance type belonging to the ecs.t5 family, designed for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that experience occasional spikes in demand. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 2 virtual CPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 core with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.t5-c1m4.large delivers entry-level performance across compute and memory subsystems. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 2090.03. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with large-block read speeds at 16.3 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.44 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 870.0 and a multi-core score of 1493.0, reflecting the performance limitations inherent in its burstable CPU allocation model.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and low baseline network bandwidth, this instance is structured for budget-conscious scenarios where continuous high performance is not required. It is suitable for lightweight applications such as low-traffic web servers, development environments, code repositories, and basic microservices. The lack of bundled local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage. This profile offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent workloads, but it is unsuitable for database operations, data science, or continuous high-throughput processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a burstable, budget-oriented instance within the ecs.t5 family. It features 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 core running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data places its compute and memory performance in the lower tiers, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1493.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 2090.03. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block write speeds at 14.44 GB/sec. Because of its burstable CPU allocation and low baseline performance, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for low-intensity, intermittent workloads. It is best suited for development environments, lightweight web serving, and small-scale testing rather than sustained database or computational tasks.
